subquestions.text_open: 10-3 The figure above is a simplified diagram of a photoredox catalytic mechanism. Such reactions use a photocatalyst capable of both single-electron oxidation and reduction under visible-light irradiation to initiate radical reactions and, after a series of complex steps, quench the radical process. 10-3-1 Based on the information above, write the SMILES structures of the 3 key intermediates in the reaction shown and of the other product in addition to the product depicted. PMP denotes p-methoxyphenyl.

text_images.description: Schematic of a photocatalyst quenching cycle. “P-Cat” is at the bottom center and “P-Cat*” at the top, with an upward vertical arrow between them labeled “hν.” Blue circular arrows connect “P-Cat*,” “P-Cat^+•,” “P-Cat^-•,” and “P-Cat”: the left blue arrow points downward from P-Cat* to P-Cat^+•, and the lower-left blue arrow points down and right from P-Cat^+• to P-Cat; the right blue arrow points downward from P-Cat* to P-Cat^-•, and the lower-right blue arrow points down and left from P-Cat^-• to P-Cat. “Oxidative Quenching” is labeled at the upper left, near “A” and “A^-•,” with a curved red arrow from A to A^-•. At the lower left are “D” and “D^+•,” with a curved red arrow from D to D^+•. “Reductive Quenching” is labeled at the upper right, near “D” and “D^+•,” with a curved red arrow from D to D^+•. At the lower right are “A” and “A^-•,” with a curved red arrow from A to A^-•.
